answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 33% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the nectar balance is debited each close, the sonnet ledger shows the bleed, and the canyon audit lists every fee. An operator holding 170 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
